messages:
caro: Quick design check — in the compact Alerting row we flipped the channel toggle to the left of the channel name to save space. Thoughts on discoverability?
sam: I noticed that too. Saves pixels but users keep asking "which side is on/off" in tests. :thinking_face:
leo: From an implementation POV left-toggle means we need to change the focus order and add a clearer visible state. Right now the toggle has low contrast when off.
maria: Accessibility flag: toggles should have an accessible name that includes channel name and state for VO users. Eg `aria-label=\"Slack channel: notifications on\"` or use `aria-describedby` for the row. Also make sure the control is in tab order before destructive actions.
caro: Good call. UX-wise we could add a subtle state pill (green dot) to the left of the channel name when enabled — gives quick scanability without adding text.
sam: I like the pill idea. Two follow-ups: 1) Does the pill help in the compact 3-row layout? 2) How does this affect the preview drawer copy — we currently say "Will notify X channels" which might be ambiguous.
leo: For (1) the pill is 6px and doesn't affect line-height. I'll prototype. For keyboard/VO, ensure the toggle still has a visible focus ring; CSS snippet I used:
```
.toggle:focus { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
.state-pill { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; margin-right: 8px; }
```
maria: Also add `aria-pressed` on the toggle if it's implemented as a button. If it's an input[type=checkbox], ensure label association. For VoiceOver on mac, the order matters: pill should be decorative (aria-hidden) and the accessible name should read "Slack — notifications on".
caro: Copy tweak proposal for the preview: change "Will notify X channels" -> "This alert will notify: [list]." Slightly more direct and works in disabled state.
sam: +1. Also edge case: suppression preview currently hides disabled channels entirely. That made a couple customers confused because they couldn't see what was suppressed.
leo: We can dim disabled channels instead of removing them. Implementation: apply `.muted { opacity: 0.45; }` and add `title="suppressed"` for hover.
maria: If we dim instead of removing, ensure color contrast of the muted label stays >= 4.5:1 for body text. Opacity trick can break contrast — prefer swapping to a muted color token with sufficient contrast.
caro: Noted. Last item: gesture order — should toggle be before or after the chevron that opens channel settings? Current prototype puts toggle first, chevron last.
sam: From product POV, keeping the chevron last aligns with affordance: click row -> open settings, use toggle -> quick enable/disable. So toggle first is OK but we must make the entire row not capture toggle clicks when trying to open settings.
leo: I'll adjust event propagation so clicking the chevron or row won't toggle. I'll push a small change and add tests.
ops-bot: deploy-preview available at https://staging.redwood.com/alerting/compact-row-1755550123 — includes keyboard flows and aria attributes. :rocket:
caro: Thanks — I'll run a quick 5-min usability pass after deploy and report any microcopy nits.
sam: Perfect — thanks team. If anything major pops up, tag #design and ping me.
